spans.s: दिव् (I) vt. or vi. (pp. द्यूत or द्यून; pres. दीव्यति; desid. दुधूषति, दिदेविषति) 1. To shine; 2. to throw, to cast (as a missile), Bt.xvii.87, v.81; 3. to gamble, to play (in this sense, दिव् governs the acc. or inst., e.g. अक्षैः or अक्षान् दीव्यति); 4. to trifle with, to make sport of; 5. to deal in transactions, to stake, to sell, (with a gen.), अदेवीद्बंधुभोगानाम् Bt.viii.122; (but when preceded by a preposition it is used with an acc. or gen., e.g. शतस्य or शतं प्रतिदीव्यति); 6. to praise; 7. to be glad, to rejoice; 8. to be mad or drunk; 8. to be sleepy; 10. to wish for.
दिव् (II) vt. 1P, 10U (pres. देवति, देवयति-ते) To cause to lament, to pain, to vex.
दिव् (III) vi. 10Ā (pres. देवयते) To suffer pain, to lament.With परि-, to lament, to suffer pain, Bt.iv.34.
दिव् f. (nom. sing. द्यौः) 1. The heaven, R.iii.4, 12, Megh.ii.30; 2. the sky; 3. a day.
दिवस्पति m. an epithet of Indra, अनतिक्रमणीया दिवस्पतेराज्ञा Sak.vi.
दिवस्पृथिव्यौ f. du. the heaven and earth.
दिविज m. a god.
दिविष्ठ m. an inhabitant of the sky, a god.

दिवोकस् m. a god, R.iii.19, 47, Sak.vii.
दिव n. 1. Heaven; 2. the sky; 3. a day; 4. a forest.
दिवा ind. By day, in the day time.(दिवाभू ‘to become day’ e.g. दिवाभूता रात्रिः.)
दिवस m.n. A day, दिवसाः परिणामरमणीयाः Sak.i., Am.
दिवस-ईश्वर, -कर m. the sun, Rt.iii.22.
दिवस-ईश्वर, -कर m. the sun, Rt.iii.22.
दिवस-मुख n. day-break.
दिवस-विगम m. evening, sunset, Megh.ii.16.
दिवा-अटन m. a crow.
दिवा-अंध m. an owl.
दिवा-अंधकी, -अंधिका f. the musk-rat.
दिवा-अंधकी, -अंधिका f. the musk-rat.
दिवा-कर m. 1. the sun, R.xix.8, K.S.i.12, v.48; 2. a crow; 3. the sun-flower.
दिवा-कीर्ति m. 1. a man of low caste; 2. a barber; 3. an owl.
दिवा-तन a. belonging to the day, K.S.iv.36, Bt.v.65.
दिवा-निशम् f. day and night.
दिवा-प्रदीप m. a lamp by day, i.e. an obscure man.
दिवा-भीत, -भीति m. 1. an owl, See K.S.i.12; 2. a thief, a house-breaker.
दिवा-भीत, -भीति m. 1. an owl, See K.S.i.12; 2. a thief, a house-breaker.
दिवा-मध्य n. mid-day.
दिवा-रात्रम् ind. day and night.
दिवा-वसु m. the sun.
दिवा-शय a. sleeping at day, R.xix.34.
दिवा-स्वप्न, -स्वाप m. sleep during day-time.
दिवा-स्वप्न, -स्वाप m. sleep during day-time.
दिवि m. The chāsha bird. (Also दिव m.)
दिव्य (I) a. (f. व्या) 1. Divine, heavenly; 2. supernatural, wonderful (as in दिव्यचक्षुस्), Bg.xi.8; 3. charming, beautiful.
दिव्य (II) m. 1. A superhuman being, दिव्यानामपि कृतविस्मयां पुरस्तात् Sis.viii.64; 2. barley; 3. an epithet of Yama; 4. a philosopher.
दिव्य (III) n. 1. Celestial nature, divinity; 2. an ordeal (of which ten kinds are enumerated); 3. the sky; 4. an oath, a solemn declaration; 5. cloves; 6. a kind of sandal.
दिव्य (I) a. (f. व्या) 1. Divine, heavenly; 2. supernatural, wonderful (as in दिव्यचक्षुस्), Bg.xi.8; 3. charming, beautiful.
दिव्य-अंशु m. the sun.
दिव्य-अंगना, -नारी, -स्त्री f. a divine woman, an Apsaras, a nymph.

दिव्य-अदिव्य a. partly human and partly divine (as a hero in a poetic composition), K.Pr.vii.
दिव्य-उदक n. rain-water.
दिव्य-कारिन् a. 1. taking an oath; 2. undergoing an ordeal.
दिव्य-गायन m. a Gandharva.
दिव्य-चक्षुस् (I) m. a monkey.
दिव्य-चक्षुस् (II) n. prophetic or supernatural vision, the faculty of seeing what is invisible by the human eye.
दिव्य-चक्षुस् (III) a. 1. one possessing such vision, R.iii.45; 2. blind.
दिव्य-ज्ञान n. supernatural knowledge.
दिव्य-दृश् m. an astrologer.
दिव्य-प्रश्न m. inquiring into the future course of events, augury.
दिव्य-मानुष m. a demi-god.
दिव्य-रत्न n. a fabulous gem supposed to grant all desires of its possessor, the philosopher’s stone. See चिंतामणि.
दिव्य-रथ m. a celestial car moving through the air.
दिव्य-रस m. quick-silver.
दिव्य-वस्त्र m. sunshine.
दिव्य-सरित् f. the celestial Ganges.
दिव्य-सार m. the Sāla tree.
